checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate but require refinement on the 'Ears' checkpoint. The Router marked 'Ears... carried close to head' as false because they hang down. While technically true that they aren't folded back, Rhodesian Ridgebacks do have drop ears; 'carried close' usually refers to them lying flat against the cheek rather than sticking out. The image shows them hanging naturally, which is acceptable, so I will adjust this to 'Present' with a note on slight laxity. The 'Ridge' checkpoint is correctly marked N/A due to occlusion. The 'Legs' and 'Tail' are also correctly N/A. The Router was too lenient on the 'Gait' checkpoint by marking it untestable; while the dog is sitting, the muscular definition visible in the shoulders supports the 'powerful' aspect of the gait description, but strictly speaking, gait is dynamic, so N/A is safer. I agree with the Router's assessment of the Head and Coat.

I agree with the severity ratings but note that the 'structural collapse' in the muzzle is more likely a focus/depth-of-field issue or minor generative softness rather than a catastrophic defect. The Perceptual Quality Auditor found no global distortions, which is consistent with a high-quality generation.
